clue.text: Settled problem about paper used in chemistry test

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned about, so the word for problem faces the other way

blocks.note: a bird that has settled has lit, the past tense of alight
a sum is an arithmetic problem set at school

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher has resolved a difficulty with the paper needed for an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper changes colour to show whether a solution is acid or alkaline, the classic school laboratory test.

clue.text: Shots for effect one girl receives bring respite at last

indicators.note: 'at last' asks for the final letter of each of the two words
the girl receives, so takes inside her, the selected letters

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a common girl's name
the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Injections to relieve pain are given to a woman, finally bringing her some respite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' looks medical, but means photographs or camera shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is the set of pictures or visual images used, in film or writing, to produce an effect.

clue.text: Lore shows goodness — Christian studies lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking says one letter is taken out of the subject

blocks.note: 'my!' and 'goodness!' are both exclamations of surprise
theology is the study of religion and doctrine
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Traditional stories reveal virtue, but religious education lacks vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology is a body of traditional stories and beliefs, which is what lore means.

clue.text: Like some buns quietly excluded from fast

indicators.note: excluded from says the letter for quiet is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
speedy means fast

explanation.surface: Some sweet rolls are quietly left out of a period of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' wants to be a noun about not eating; it is the adjective quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Some bread buns are topped with sesame or poppy seeds, so they could be described as containing seeds.

clue.text: Show less restraint in puzzle

blocks.note: first reading: to become more unruly, split as two words
second reading: to confuse or baffle someone

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning only works if the answer is split into a verb and a comparative adjective: BE WILDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to confuse them thoroughly, the same as puzzling or baffling them.

clue.text: It helps tramp to settle down

definitions.text: It helps tramp to settle down

blocks.clueFragment: It helps tramp to settle down
blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps a homeless wanderer find a permanent home
setter's reading: a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route, kept low and steady in the water by heavy material

explanation.walkthrough: A tramp steamer is a freighter that picks up cargo wherever it can; weight in the hold makes it sit lower in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy material carried in a ship's hold to improve stability makes the vessel ride lower and steadier.

clue.text: Place to relax in annexe one enters daily

indicators.note: one enters, so goes inside, the word for daily

blocks.note: a wing is an extension of a building
a daily is a British cleaning lady, also called a char
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A house extension is somewhere to unwind, visited every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily, short for daily help, is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing chair is a high-backed armchair with side pieces, a comfortable seat to relax in.

clue.text: Charges excessive amount?

blocks.note: first meaning: fills, as one charges a gun or a vehicle
second meaning: an informal word for lots

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at a surface about overcharging; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To load a gun is to charge it, and informally a great many of something is described as plenty or a lot.

clue.text: Offers from pressman banking twenty shillings

indicators.note: banking means keeping safe inside, so the journalist holds the money

blocks.note: ed is short for editor, a newspaperman
X is the Roman ten, and ten more makes twenty
s was the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: A journalist making bids while pocketing a pound in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty shillings made a pound; here twenty is split into two tens, one Roman and one in words.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or a hand is to offer it, so extends and offers are synonyms.

clue.text: Bin stealer shot in Soviet sector once

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A thief raiding rubbish bins is gunned down in a Cold War city.
explanation.definitionFit: After 1945 the eastern part of the German capital was the zone occupied by the Soviet Union, later capital of East Germany.

clue.text: Books in excellent political opponent

indicators.note: 'in' places the books inside the word for excellent

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Fine writing by someone who argues against a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI in crosswords, the digit standing in for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person opposed to a policy or party, so a political opponent in noun form.

clue.text: Wrong iron taken by heartless nutter

indicators.note: without a heart, the word for nutter loses one of its central letters

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a loony is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A golf iron or clothes iron seized by a madman, which is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: LOONY has a doubled O at its centre; dropping one of them leaves LONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime, and a wrong is a noun meaning an unlawful or unjust act.

clue.text: Bill with copper and grass pointing finger

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to grass and to sing are both slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A police officer and an informer point the finger at a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and copper both look like police slang, but here one is an account and the other a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing the finger at somebody is an idiom for blaming them, which is exactly what an accusing person does.

clue.text: One spell for rookie in duty roster

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A newcomer is given one shift on the rota of duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or novice, the same as a rookie new to a job.

clue.text: Bizarre boor's left behind an attractive person

indicators.note: the left-hand letter of the boor is sent behind, moving from the front to the back

blocks.note: a lout is a rough, uncouth man
taken as written
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: An oaf has been abandoned for a good-looking partner, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left is both part of LOUT and the letter being moved, giving OUTL.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish describes something weird or unconventional, so bizarre is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Standard e-mail from Dicky

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters need fixing into order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An ordinary message sent by a man called Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky, capitalised to look like a name, is British slang meaning shaky or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the French kings, so a flag or standard carried into battle.

clue.text: Syrian female taking a view

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a female parent
taken as written
a scene is a view or vista

explanation.surface: A woman from Syria admires the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene means from Damascus, the capital of Syria, so it serves as an adjective for a Syrian thing or person.

clue.text: Comparatively small MP perhaps needs minder

blocks.note: baby as an adjective means a smaller version, as in baby carrots
an MP sits in Parliament, so is one who sits

explanation.surface: A minor politician needs a bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like it wants an abbreviation, but here it is a member who sits in the House.
explanation.definitionFit: A babysitter looks after children while parents are out, so a minder in the childcare sense.

clue.text: This bridge needs care shown with maximum speed lowered

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowered means the letter moves further down the word

blocks.note: caution means care or wariness
c, the speed of light, names the letter already in the word above that is moved, adding nothing new

explanation.surface: A bridge needs careful driving with the speed limit reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Maximum speed is c, the speed of light; that C at the top of the word for care drops two places down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is the card game that came before contract bridge, so this bridge is one form of the game.

clue.text: Exploding stew pot creates dance

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A casserole dish bursts in the kitchen and sends everyone jumping about.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom or country dance with sliding steps in duple time.

clue.text: Hounds assembly that was correct

blocks.note: first meaning: the gathering of riders and dogs before a hunt
second meaning: an old word for proper or fitting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' marks the second meaning as archaic: the word once meant right, as in 'it is meet and right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox hunt begins at the meet, and in older English meet meant suitable or proper.

clue.text: Promote team though one short at breaks

indicators.note: one short says a single letter is missing from the end of the team
the small word breaks into the team, splitting it apart

blocks.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players
taken as written

explanation.surface: A side moves up a division despite playing a man down at times.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise them in rank, the same as promoting them.

clue.text: Coal processed outside top university in Mexican city

indicators.note: something processed has been worked over and changed, so these letters are reordered
'outside' puts the rearranged fuel around the following pieces

blocks.note: the four letters to rearrange
a cap is a top or lid
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Fuel is refined at a leading university somewhere in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort and port on Mexico's Pacific coast, a well-known city of that country.

clue.text: Annoy class in gym the day before

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is the school lesson held in the gym
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: Being irritated by a gym lesson the day before something.
explanation.definitionFit: To peeve is to irritate or vex someone, so it is a verb meaning the same as annoy.

clue.text: Indy and ES to merge? That's animating American!

indicators.note: merging blends the two groups together into one new arrangement

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange, ignoring 'and'

explanation.surface: A question about two companies combining, with a hint at an American cartoon empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is just a joiner between the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney was the American producer behind Mickey Mouse and the great animated feature films.

clue.text: Detective Sergeant stores booze in barrels

indicators.note: to store is to hold inside, so the officer wraps round the drink

blocks.note: DS is the standard abbreviation for the rank
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A police officer keeps alcohol in casks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drums are cylindrical containers for liquids, so they are barrels in the sense of storage vessels.

clue.text: So many women in exquisite clothes

indicators.note: read as a verb, 'clothes' means the words wrap around the letters wanted

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A count of women wearing lovely outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun about dresses, but it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So many' stands for a number in crossword style, and nine is one such quantity.

clue.text: Old man has severe fatigue so fit to lie back

indicators.note: lying back means the word for fit is laid down the other way round

blocks.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is chronic fatigue syndrome
thus means so or therefore
hale means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: An exhausted elderly man is told he is well enough to recline.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived man, so his name is used for any very old man.

clue.text: Badly want guard patrols very involved

indicators.note: a guard who patrols an area goes round it, so surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: to keep is to guard or protect
to need is to want badly

explanation.surface: Sentries keep watch over an area where there is great desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knee-deep in something is an idiom for being deeply engaged or caught up in it.

clue.text: Set rocky disc on first audio device

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the three letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the three letters to rearrange
re means on or about, as in a letter heading
O is a disc by its round shape

explanation.surface: A record is placed on a shaky turntable to play music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc on first' means the word for on comes before the disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system that plays music through two channels, a common piece of audio equipment.
